# Documentation Standards

Follow these documentation practices to maintain clarity and help future contributors.

## Code Documentation

- Write JSDoc comments for exported functions and components
- Document complex algorithms or business logic
- Include usage examples for utility functions
- Document prop types with descriptions
- Explain "why" not just "what" in comments

## Component Documentation

- Document component purpose and usage
- List and describe all props with types
- Provide usage examples for complex components
- Document any special behaviors or edge cases
- Note accessibility considerations

## README Files

- Include project overview and purpose
- Document setup and installation steps
- List available scripts and their purposes
- Provide contribution guidelines
- Include troubleshooting tips

## API Documentation

- Document all API endpoints
- Specify request and response formats
- Include example requests and responses
- Document error codes and handling
- Note authentication requirements

## Inline Comments

- Use comments to explain complex logic
- Avoid obvious comments that restate code
- Keep comments up-to-date with code changes
- Use TODO comments for future improvements
- Mark temporary hacks with HACK or FIXME

## Markdown Best Practices

- Use proper heading hierarchy
- Include code blocks with language syntax
- Use lists for better readability
- Add links to related documentation
- Include visual aids (diagrams, screenshots) when helpful

## Documentation Structure

- Keep documentation close to the code
- Organize docs in a logical hierarchy
- Use consistent formatting and style
- Update docs as part of code changes
- Review docs during code review process
